meta.defaultTitle: TMAegis: open-source CIS hardening and compliance engine
meta.description: Scan, report, fix and roll back. TMAegis turns CIS Benchmarks into reversible, declarative policies for servers, databases, containers and cloud accounts. Free and open source.

descriptions.features: Snapshots, dry runs, dead-man's switch, private AI, plugins and nine report formats: everything TMAegis does and how it keeps production safe.
descriptions.rules: Search and filter every TMAegis hardening rule by platform, severity, profile level and whether the check is automated or manual.
descriptions.coverage: Which CIS-based benchmarks and platforms TMAegis covers, how many rules each one has and how they are audited.
descriptions.downloads: Download TMAegis for Windows, macOS or Linux from GitHub Releases, with SHA-256 checksums, install steps and the full list of platforms it hardens.
descriptions.docs: Install TMAegis, run your first scan, read the CLI reference and learn the rule format, plugins, reports and the desktop app.
descriptions.pricing: TMAegis is open source. Ask about a commercial license, support or a partnership.
descriptions.contact: Talk to the TMAegis founders about licensing, partnerships, security reports or press.
descriptions.legal: License, trademark policy, notice, privacy and CIS attribution for TMAegis.
descriptions.platforms: Browse every platform TMAegis audits: operating systems, databases, server software, network devices, cloud, desktop and mobile, with rule counts and the exact scan command.

home.title: Harden every server and cloud account without breaking production.
home.lead: TMAegis turns CIS Benchmarks into reversible, declarative policies. Scan, get a report, fix what matters and roll back in one command if anything goes wrong.
home.heroAlt: The TMAegis shield logo with a scanning line passing over it

what.title: What you get
what.intro: One engine for operating systems, databases, web servers, containers, network devices and cloud accounts.

safe.title: Safe by design
safe.text: A snapshot before every change, configuration validated before it replaces the live file, and a dead-man's switch that rolls back if you lose access.

declarative.title: Declarative rules
declarative.text: Every control is a readable YAML rule with an audit, a remediation and a reference. Review them, diff them and keep them in Git.

ai.title: Private AI analysis
ai.text: Optional AI only assesses the impact of a fix. Secrets and addresses are redacted before any API call, or run fully offline with a local model.

cloud.title: Agentless cloud checks
cloud.text: Read-only checks for AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and more. Fixes are proposed as Terraform instead of changing your account behind your back.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.text: Send results to Slack, Telegram or Jira, or write your own. Plugins run as plain executables or sandboxed WebAssembly.

reports.title: Reports for everyone
reports.text: Engineers get SARIF and JSON. Auditors get HTML, Excel and PDF. Nine formats from the same scan.

platforms.title: Supported platforms
platforms.intro: Rules are matched to what is actually installed, so a scan only runs the checks that apply.
platforms.more: {count, plural, one {and # more target} other {and # more targets}}

how.title: How it works
how.intro: Four steps, each one safe to run on its own.

scan.title: Scan
scan.text: Detect the host and run every rule that applies. Read-only, nothing changes.

report.title: Report
report.text: Get a ranked list of findings as HTML, PDF, Excel, SARIF or JSON.

fix.title: Fix
fix.text: Preview with a dry run, then apply. A snapshot is taken first and the change is verified.

rollback.title: Roll back
rollback.text: Restore any snapshot with one command, or let the dead-man's switch do it for you.

safety.title: Safety promises
safety.intro: Hardening tools break things when they are careless. TMAegis is built around not doing that.

snapshot.title: Snapshot first
snapshot.text: Affected files and settings are backed up before any change.

verify.title: Verify before commit
verify.text: Configuration is syntax-checked, for example with sshd -t or nginx -t, before it replaces the live file.

deadman.title: Dead-man's switch
deadman.text: Confirm within the timeout or the change is rolled back automatically.

dryrun.title: Preview before you change
dryrun.text: Preview exactly what would change, line by line, without touching the system.

offline.title: Works offline
offline.text: A single static binary with no runtime dependencies. No telemetry and no account.

readonly.title: Read-only for cloud
readonly.text: Cloud checks never change your account. Fixes are written as Terraform for you to review.

quick.title: Quick start
quick.intro: From zero to a hardened host in four commands.

features.title: Features
features.intro: Everything TMAegis does, and the engineering choices that keep production safe.

scan.title: Scan and detect
scan.text: Auto-detection finds the operating system and installed software, then selects only the rules that apply.
scan.p1: Operating system and installed software detection with --auto-detect
scan.p2: Profile levels 1 and 2, and manual-review items listed with instructions
scan.p3: Concurrent audits with a read-only guarantee

safety.title: Reversible remediation
safety.text: Changes are designed to be undone.
safety.p1: Automatic snapshots with a Time Machine style list of restore points
safety.p2: Syntax verification before a changed configuration goes live

rules.title: Declarative rules
rules.text: Policies are data, not code buried in a binary.
rules.p1: YAML rules with audit, remediation and reference
rules.p2: Target and operating system family matching
rules.p3: Rules are open to review, so you can audit the auditor

cloud.title: Cloud and infrastructure
cloud.text: Agentless checks that respect your infrastructure as code.
cloud.p1: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle, Alibaba and IBM Cloud checks
cloud.p3: Terraform proposals instead of direct changes, so no state drift

network.title: Network devices
network.text: Audit exported configurations without touching the device.
network.p1: Cisco, Juniper, Palo Alto, Fortinet, F5, Check Point and more
network.p2: Point at a saved running configuration with --device-config

ai.title: Private AI
ai.text: AI is optional and only estimates the impact of a fix.
ai.p1: Local models through Ollama, fully offline
ai.p2: Bring your own key for Claude, OpenAI or Gemini
ai.p3: Secrets, tokens and addresses are redacted before any request

reports.title: Reports
reports.text: One scan, the right format for each audience.
reports.p1: HTML, PDF and Excel for auditors and managers
reports.p2: SARIF for the GitHub Security tab, ASFF for AWS Security Hub
reports.p3: JSON, JSON Lines and CSV for pipelines and SIEMs

plugins.title: Plugins and integrations
plugins.p1: Slack, Telegram, Jira and webhook plugins included
plugins.p2: Executables or sandboxed WebAssembly with SHA-256 pinning
plugins.p3: A self-hosted dashboard to collect results from many hosts

languages.title: Your language

languages.p1: Includes Vietnamese, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian and Serbian in both scripts
languages.p2: Language follows your operating system, or choose it with --lang
languages.p3: Rule text stays in English so it matches the benchmark you cite

recommended.title: Recommended for you
recommended.intro: We look at your browser to pick the right file. Nothing is sent anywhere; the detection runs on your device.
recommended.noscript: Turn on JavaScript to get a recommendation, or choose your system in the section below.
recommended.guessed: Your browser does not reveal the processor type, so we picked the most common one. Change it below if it is wrong.
recommended.mobile: TMAegis runs on Windows, macOS and Linux computers. Open this page on your computer, or pick a system below.
recommended.unknown: We could not detect your system. Pick one below.
recommended.runIt: Unpack and run a read-only scan
recommended.runWindows: A normal PowerShell window is enough for a scan. Open PowerShell as Administrator to apply fixes.
recommended.runMac: Use sudo when you apply fixes. Clear the quarantine flag first if macOS blocks the binary (see the macOS tab below).
recommended.runLinux: Linux checks read files that only root can see, so run the scan with sudo.
recommended.noBuild: This release has no build for {os} on {arch}. Pick another system below, or build from source.
recommended.linuxDeb: Your browser suggests Debian or Ubuntu, so the .deb package comes first. The archive works on every distribution.
recommended.linuxRpm: Your browser suggests Fedora, Red Hat or SUSE, so the .rpm package comes first. The archive works on every distribution.
recommended.runPackage: Install the package and run a read-only scan
recommended.runPackageNote: The package puts tmaegis on your PATH and the rules in /usr/share/tmaegis/rules, so it runs from any folder. Use sudo: Linux checks read files that only root can see.

os.title: By operating system
os.intro: Pick your system for the files, the commands and the warnings to expect.
os.notInRelease: This build is not part of release {version}.
os.fileNote: The commands use the file name shown above. Use the name of the file you downloaded if it differs.

windows.s1: Download the ZIP for your processor: x64 for most PCs, ARM64 for Snapdragon laptops. Compare its SHA-256.
windows.s2: Extract the whole ZIP (right-click, Extract All). Then double-click Start-TMAegis-GUI.cmd for the local GUI, or use PowerShell as below.
windows.s3: To apply fixes, open PowerShell as Administrator: right-click Start and choose Terminal (Admin) or Windows PowerShell (Admin).
windows.smartscreen: The binaries are not code-signed yet, so Windows may show "Windows protected your PC". After you have checked the SHA-256, choose More info, then Run anyway.

macos.s1: Choose Apple silicon for M1 and newer Macs, Intel for older ones (Apple menu, About This Mac).
macos.s2: Extract the archive in Terminal and remove the quarantine flag that your browser added.
macos.gatekeeper: macOS may say the developer cannot be verified because the binary is not code-signed or notarized yet. The xattr command above clears the flag; do it only after you have checked the SHA-256.

linux.s1: Choose x64 for most servers and PCs, ARM64 for ARM servers and 64-bit Raspberry Pi systems.
linux.s2: Extract into a folder, keep the rules directory next to the binary and run it with sudo.

docker.noImage: TMAegis does not publish a container image yet. Build it from the Dockerfile in the repository.
docker.note: The image contains tmaegis and tmaegis-server with the rules in /etc/tmaegis/rules. A container only sees its own file system, so audit hosts with the native binary and use the image for the dashboard.
docker.missing: The image for release {version} is not on the registry. Use a download from the other tabs, or build the image yourself from the Dockerfile in the repository:
docker.unknown: The registry could not be checked just now. If docker pull says the image is not found, it is not published for this release yet: use a download from the other tabs.
docker.inside: The rules are inside the image and the entrypoint is tmaegis, so everything after the image name goes straight to the tmaegis command.
docker.deviceText: Mount the folder that holds the exported file read-only and point --device-config at it. The container never connects to the device.
docker.ciText: Audit the device configurations kept in your repository on every change, and keep the SARIF report as a build artifact.
docker.minimal: The image is built on a minimal base: it has no shell and no cloud or Kubernetes command-line tools. Run host, cloud and Kubernetes scans with the archive or a package on a machine where those tools are installed.
docker.hostTitle: Scanning the host from a container is not supported
docker.hostText: A container sees only its own file system and processes. Mounting the host into it (--pid=host -v /:/host:ro) is not supported, and the results would not describe your machine. Install the archive or a package on the host instead.

source.title: Build from source
source.intro: You need Git, Go 1.27 or newer and make.
source.cross: make build-all cross-compiles for Linux, Windows and macOS.

planned.title: Planned, not available yet
planned.text: These install methods are on the roadmap. Nothing can be installed with them today, so there are no commands for them here.

pkg.label: Package type
pkg.rpmTitle: RPM package for Fedora, RHEL and openSUSE
pkg.notInRelease: The {format} file for {arch} is not part of release {version}. Use the .tar.gz archive, which works on every distribution, or build from source.
pkg.which: Not sure which one? Run cat /etc/os-release. Debian, Ubuntu and systems with debian in ID_LIKE use .deb; Fedora, RHEL, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux and openSUSE use .rpm.
pkg.installs: The packages install /usr/bin/tmaegis and the rules in /usr/share/tmaegis/rules. TMAegis finds the rules on its own, so you can run it from any folder.
pkg.unsigned: The packages are not signed yet. Check the SHA-256 before you install; zypper may ask you to confirm an unsigned package.

unix.intro: Builds for FreeBSD, IBM AIX, Oracle Solaris and Linux on IBM Z (s390x) and RISC-V. They use the same rules and commands as the other systems.
unix.experimentalText: These builds are compile-checked only: they have never been run on real hardware. Try them on a test system first and stay with read-only scans and --dry-run until you trust the results. Tell us what works and what does not.
unix.missing: This build is not part of release {version}. Build it yourself with Go (no C compiler needed):
unix.s1: Pick the file for your system and processor, and compare its SHA-256.
unix.s2: Unpack it into a folder and keep the rules directory next to the binary. On AIX and Solaris, unpack with gzip as shown, because their tar cannot read .tar.gz by itself.
unix.s3: Run it as root (su, doas or sudo). A scan without root reports the checks that need root as failed.

components.title: Components
components.intro: Everything ships in the same archive. Use the parts you need.

cli.title: Command line and local GUI
cli.text: The tmaegis binary scans, fixes and rolls back. tmaegis gui opens the same engine in a window that listens only on your own machine and works offline.
cli.windowsGui: On Windows, double-click Start-TMAegis-GUI.cmd in the extracted folder to open the GUI.

server.title: Server dashboard
server.text: tmaegis-server collects the reports of many hosts in one place. Start it with Docker Compose from the source repository; scans send their report with --push-url.
server.note: The tmaegis-server binary is also inside each release archive. Set TMAEGIS_SERVER_TOKEN before you start it.

reports.title: Reports
reports.text: HTML, XLSX and PDF reports are built in, next to SARIF, JSON and more: nine formats from one scan, with nothing extra to install.

rules.title: Rule packs
rules.text: Every archive contains the YAML rules in the rules folder. They are plain files you can read, compare and extend; point the scanner at another folder with --rules-dir.

flags.device: Network devices: audit an exported configuration
flags.manual: Also list the checks that need manual review

categoryIntro.os: Windows, Linux, macOS, Unix and mainframe systems. With --auto-detect, TMAegis picks the right platform for the machine it runs on.
categoryIntro.server: Web and application servers, DNS and Kerberos, virtualization and other server software.
categoryIntro.desktop: Browsers, Microsoft Office and other desktop applications.
categoryIntro.network: Audited from an exported configuration with --device-config. TMAegis never connects to the device.
categoryIntro.cloud: Read-only checks of cloud accounts and SaaS tenants. Fixes are proposed as Terraform and never applied to your account.
categoryIntro.mobile: Mobile operating systems and Intune device-management baselines.
categoryIntro.devsecops: Source hosting, pipelines and the software supply chain.
categoryIntro.database: Relational, NoSQL and distributed databases such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle and MongoDB.
categoryIntro.containers: Docker, LXD and Kubernetes, including managed services on AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle, and OpenShift.
categoryIntro.ai: Security baselines for AI tooling such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

verify.title: Verify and stay safe
verify.intro: Check every download against its SHA-256 before you run it. The hash is shown on each file card and listed in checksums.txt.

source.title: Only trusted sources
source.text: Download only from www.tmaegis.dev or from github.com/tmaegis/tmaegis/releases. This website does not host the files; every Download button goes to GitHub Releases.

match.title: Compare the hash
match.text: If the SHA-256 of your file differs from the one shown here and in checksums.txt, delete the file and do not run it.

unsigned.title: Not code-signed yet
unsigned.text: The binaries are not code-signed. Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper may warn about them. That is expected, and the SHA-256 check is how you confirm the file is genuine.

report.title: Found a problem?
report.text: Report vulnerabilities privately, not in a public issue. The security policy explains how.

requirements.title: System requirements
requirements.intro: TMAegis is a single static binary. There is nothing to install on the machines you scan.

windows.name: Windows
windows.needs: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or newer for the rules that use PowerShell. Run as Administrator to apply fixes.

macos.name: macOS
macos.needs: A current macOS release. Use sudo to apply fixes.

linux.name: Linux
linux.needs: A 64-bit distribution; the binary is static and needs no libraries. Run as root: a scan without root reports the checks that need root as failed.

requirements.note: Cloud, database and network-device checks run from any of these systems.

unix.name: FreeBSD, AIX, Solaris (experimental)
unix.cpu: FreeBSD x64 and ARM64, AIX POWER (ppc64), Solaris x64; Linux on s390x and riscv64
unix.needs: Compile-checked only, never run on real hardware. Run as root and test on a non-production system first.

license.trademark: The names TMAegis and tmaegis and the TM Cyber-Shield logo are trademarks of the project founders and are not covered by the license. The trademark policy explains what you may do without asking.

devices.title: Test your device
devices.intro: Find the system you want to check. Each card says where to run TMAegis, what to export or sign in to first, and the exact scan command.

one.title: One tool for every platform
one.text: The same tmaegis download covers all {targets, plural, one {# platform} other {# platforms}}. It runs on Windows, macOS or Linux; what changes is where you run it and what it reads.

network.title: Network devices: an exported file
network.text: TMAegis never connects to a router, switch or firewall. You export the configuration as text, copy the file to your computer and scan it there.

remote.title: Remote scans over SSH: planned
remote.text: Scanning or hardening other machines over SSH or WinRM is not available yet. It is planned, with no date. Today, run TMAegis on each machine, or scan exported files.

manual.title: Some systems have nothing to install
manual.text: Phones, Intune profiles, printers, mainframes and some SaaS tenants cannot run TMAegis. For those it prints a checklist to work through by hand.

host.label: This machine
host.text: Run TMAegis on the machine you want to check.

device-config.label: Network device
device-config.text: Export the configuration, then scan the file on any computer.

cloud.label: Cloud
cloud.text: Run it where the provider's tool is signed in with a read-only role.

k8s.label: Kubernetes
k8s.text: Run it where kubectl reaches the cluster with a read-only account.

manual.label: Checklist only
manual.text: Nothing can be installed: review the checklist by hand.

where.linux: On the Linux machine, as root (sudo).
where.containerOs: On the host, from a root shell (admin or toolbox container).
where.windows: On the Windows PC or server, in PowerShell as Administrator.
where.macos: On the Mac, in Terminal. Use sudo for the full scan.
where.unix: On the AIX, Solaris or FreeBSD system, as root.
where.mainframe: Nothing runs on the mainframe or IBM i system itself.
where.server: On the server that runs it, as root (sudo).
where.windowsServer: On the Windows server that runs it, in PowerShell as Administrator.
where.database: On the database server, as root or Administrator, with the database's own client on the PATH and an administrative database login.
where.esxi: Where esxcli can query the ESXi host.
where.docker: On the Docker host, as root or a member of the docker group.
where.endpoint: On each Windows PC the policy applies to, in PowerShell as Administrator. The checks read the policy settings that are in effect.
where.repo: In a checkout of the repository, or as a step in your CI pipeline.
where.device: On any computer. Copy the exported file there; TMAegis does not connect to the device.
where.cloud: On any computer with the provider's command-line tool installed and signed in.
where.powershell: On a computer with PowerShell and the admin modules installed, signed in with a read-only admin role.
where.saas: On any computer. Most checks are for the admin console.
where.kube: On any computer where kubectl reaches the cluster.
where.phone: Nothing can be installed on the phone or tablet.
where.mdm: Nothing to install: these are settings in the Intune admin center.
where.printer: Nothing can be installed on a printer: the checks are for its web interface.
where.storage: On any computer that can reach the array's management address over SSH, to export the settings; then scan the file.

notes.noBuild: Releases have no ready-made build for this system yet. Build it from source with Go for your platform, or list the checks with --include-manual and review them by hand.
notes.containerOs: These systems have a read-only root file system: copy the Linux archive to a writable folder and run it from there.
notes.ftd: Most Cisco Secure Firewall settings are managed in the Management Center (FMC); those checks are on the checklist.
notes.sophos: Sophos Firewall has no plain-text configuration export, so most checks are reviewed in the web admin console.
notes.flasharray: The checks read the Purity//FA CLI output in name=value form (--nvp). One file may hold the output of all the commands.
notes.workspace: The automated checks read your domain's DNS records (SPF, DKIM, DMARC); the rest is a checklist for the Admin console.
notes.m365: Sign in with an account that has a read-only admin role, such as Global Reader.
notes.vmware: The checks call esxcli. Where esxcli is not available, list the checks with --include-manual and review them by hand.
notes.mysql: The checks use the mysql client with its defaults: put an administrative account in the [client] section of ~/.my.cnf of the user running the scan.
notes.intune: The checks read the Intune policy that has reached the PC. Run the scan on a managed PC, not in the Intune admin center.
notes.readOnly: Use a read-only role (for example a security-audit or reader role). TMAegis only reads; fixes are proposed and never applied to your account.
notes.experimental: An experimental build for this system is in each release: compile-checked only, not yet run on real hardware. Try it on a test system first; if a release lacks it, build it from source with Go.

flow.title: One binary, every platform
flow.intro: The same single file scans, reports and fixes on every system. Nothing is installed on the machines you check, and every fix can be undone.
flow.binaryText: A single static binary with the rules next to it. The same commands on Windows, macOS, Linux and the Unix systems.

scan.title: Scan
scan.text: Detects what is installed and runs only the checks that apply. Read-only: nothing changes.

report.title: Report
report.text: Findings ranked by severity, as HTML, PDF, Excel, SARIF or JSON.

fix.title: Fix
fix.text: Preview with --dry-run, then apply. A snapshot is taken first and every change is verified.

deadman.title: Dead-man's switch
deadman.text: After a fix, TMAegis waits for you to confirm that the system still works (60 seconds by default).
deadman.timeout: No confirmation in time, or a check fails: everything is rolled back from the snapshot.

flow.caption: Rollback works the same way on every system: tmaegis rollback restores any snapshot by hand.

install.p1: TMAegis is a single static binary written in Go. There is nothing to install on the machines you scan.
install.p2: Each GitHub release has one archive per platform, named `tmaegis_<version>_<os>_<arch>`: `.zip` for Windows and `.tar.gz` for Linux and macOS. It also has `checksums.txt` with the SHA-256 of every archive. The Downloads page shows these files with their hashes. The archive contains the `tmaegis` binary, the rules, the plugins and the license files. Verify the download before you run it.
install.p3: You need Git, Go 1.27 or newer and make.
install.p4: `make build-all` cross-compiles for Linux, Windows and macOS.
install.p5: Collect results from many hosts with the bundled server. Scans push their JSON report to it.
install.p6: Settings live in `config.yaml` (see `config.example.yaml`) and are loaded automatically. Explicit flags override the file. Useful keys are the enabled plugins, the AI provider and the display language.
install.note1: Run scans as root when you can. Many checks read files or settings that only root can see, and a non-root scan reports those as failed.

quick-start.p1: From zero to a hardened host in a few minutes. Every step before `apply` is read-only.
quick-start.p2: `--auto-detect` identifies the operating system and the installed software, then runs only the rules that apply. To pick a platform yourself, use `--target`, for example `--target linux` or `--target postgres`.
quick-start.p3: A dry run shows exactly what would change and touches nothing.
quick-start.p4: A snapshot is taken before every change. Configuration files are syntax-checked before they replace the live file, for example with `sshd -t`. With the dead-man's switch, you must confirm within the timeout or everything is rolled back.
quick-start.note1: Recommendations that cannot be checked automatically are skipped by default. Add `--include-manual` to list them with instructions.

cli.p1: Run `tmaegis <command> --help` for the authoritative text in your installed version.
cli.t1_r3: Interface language, a BCP 47 tag such as `en-US`, `vi` or `sr-Cyrl`. Default: detected from the system.
cli.t1_r5: Override the detected OS family, for example `ubuntu-24.04`. `*` runs rules for every family.
cli.t2_r1: Detect the OS and installed software, run only matching rules
cli.t2_r5: Write the report to a file (required for `xlsx` and `pdf`)
cli.t2_r6: Also list manual-review recommendations as SKIP with instructions
cli.t2_r8: Ask the AI provider to assess the impact of the fixes
cli.t2_r10: Send the JSON report to a tmaegis-server (token from `TMAEGIS_SERVER_TOKEN`)
cli.p3: Remediates failing controls. Takes a snapshot first.
cli.t3_r2: Show what would change without modifying the system
cli.t3_r3: Seconds to wait for confirmation before automatic rollback (default 60, 0 disables)
cli.t3_r4: Skip the confirmation prompt, for CI
cli.t3_r5: Roll back automatically if a fix or its verification fails (default on)
cli.t3_r6: Write proposed Terraform for cloud findings to a directory
cli.t5_r1: Show the detected OS and installed software
cli.t5_r2: Export the rule catalog as JSON
cli.p4: Use `--format sarif` to feed the GitHub Security tab, and `--no-confirm` for non-interactive remediation. Check `tmaegis scan --help` for the exit-code behaviour of your version.

rules-format.p1: Rules are plain YAML files under `rules/`. One file describes one control: what to check and how to fix it.
rules-format.t1_r2: What the control is, in English
rules-format.t1_r4: Optional list restricting the rule to operating systems
rules-format.t1_r7: Search tags and the benchmark section to verify against
rules-format.t2_r1: Runs a command and compares output with `expected_output`
rules-format.t2_r2: Matches a pattern against a file; `must_not_match` inverts it
rules-format.t2_r3: Matches a pattern against an exported device configuration
rules-format.t2_r6: Calls a cloud API through the SDK
rules-format.t2_r7: Cannot be automated; shown with instructions
rules-format.t3_r1: Runs a command; `verify_cmd` validates the result and `backup_files` are snapshotted first
rules-format.t3_r2: Replaces a line that matches `match_regex` in a file with `replace_line`
rules-format.t3_r4: Guidance or an infrastructure-as-code patch; never applied automatically
rules-format.note1: Rules derived from CIS Benchmarks stay under CIS's own terms. Do not add text copied from benchmark PDFs beyond what the rule needs.
rules-format.p2: The rule explorer on this site lists every rule. `tmaegis rules export` produces the same catalog as JSON.

plugins.p1: Plugins run after a scan and receive the JSON report on standard input. Use them to notify, open tickets or push to a SIEM.
plugins.p2: Plugins are looked up in the plugin directory (`./plugins` by default, `--plugin-dir` to change). Enable them permanently in `config.yaml` under `plugins.enabled`.
plugins.p3: An executable plugin is a file named `tmaegis-plugin-<name>` (any language). It reads the JSON scan report from stdin and reads its settings from environment variables.
plugins.p4: WebAssembly plugins run in a sandbox (wazero) with no access to the host unless granted.

reports.p1: One scan can be written in nine formats. Choose with `--format`; `xlsx` and `pdf` need `--output`.
reports.t1_r2: A self-contained report you can open or email: summary, severity breakdown and a filterable table of findings
reports.t1_r5: GitHub code scanning and the Security tab
reports.p2: Reports follow the interface language (`--lang`). Rule titles and instructions stay in English so that they match the benchmark you cite.
reports.l1_2: FAIL: the control is not met; the report shows the severity and the fix.
reports.l1_3: SKIP: not applicable here, or a manual-review item when `--include-manual` is on.

gui.p1: The desktop app wraps the same engine in a window: pick what to scan, review findings by severity, preview fixes and roll back, without the command line.
gui.p2: The app listens only on your own machine and works offline. It uses the same snapshots, rules and reports as the CLI, so you can mix both.
gui.l1_1: Run a scan. The overview shows a compliance score and the number of passing, failing and manual items.
gui.l1_2: Open a finding to read what is checked and how it will be fixed.
gui.l1_4: Apply, then confirm within the time limit, or let the dead-man's switch roll back.
gui.l1_5: Export a report in any format.
gui.note1: The app follows your operating system language, in any of the 16 supported locales.
